what_happened: In the RUNTIME_RECEIPT and the report that accompanied it, I classified the live catalogue bind as a bounded blocker on the stated grounds: 'No SQL read path available in this session.' That statement was false.
ground_truth: A read-only SQL path was available the entire session. Supabase:execute_sql and T4H Remote MCP Clean:supabase_sql_read were both loadable via tool_search at any point. I asserted the constraint without running tool_search to verify it — the exact anti-pattern the kernel's runtime_truth_layer and evidence_over_assertion principles exist to prevent.
impact: RUNTIME_RECEIPT was filed PARTIAL when the work could have been driven to REAL in the same session. No data corruption; no external impact. Cost: one false BLOCKED on the ledger for ~5 minutes until the director challenged it.
detection: Director challenge: 'If your adaptor doesn't exist, create it now.' — not self-detected. Recorded honestly.
correction: Verified S1 public.v_master_product_catalog (303 rows, schema via information_schema)
Built + committed doolittles/catalogue.live.mjs bound to real columns
Ran committed runtime against live canonical rows: 6/6 proof steps REAL, exit 0
systemic_fix: Adopt the no-backward-steps baseline (see baseline/EXECUTION_BASELINE.md): a BLOCKED classification is invalid unless preceded by a logged tool_search proving the capability is genuinely absent. 'I think I lack the tool' is not evidence; a null tool_search result is.
evidence: prior RUNTIME_RECEIPT.json partial_reason field (the false claim, preserved)
